key_insight: For every dimension n ≥ 4, there exists an open set of strictly convex quadratic problems where the long Barzilai–Borwein method converges but cannot be root-superlinear.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a concrete failure mode for a widely used first-order optimizer, cautioning practitioners against assuming rapid asymptotic convergence on quadratic objectives.
method: Construct an explicit positive-measure family of quadratics and initial points.
Use a computer-assisted proof of a nonresonant attracting seven-cycle in the projectivized BB dynamics (dimension 4).
Derive two-sided geometric bounds for gradient and error norms, ruling out superlinear decay.
evidence_signal: The paper reports explicit constants (ρ_min = 10^-6, ρ_max = 0.61) and two-sided geometric estimates for spectral components, gradient norm, error norm, and objective gap.
watch_item: The result is a worst-case construction for BB1 on quadratics; it does not imply typical problems will exhibit this behavior, but it does show superlinear convergence is not generic.
paper_title: Barzilai-Borwein Fails Superlinear Convergence on an Open Set of Quadratics for Every Dimension $n\geq 4$
